Single-serving One-Pan Lemon-Garlic Chicken with Potatoes and Greens

Serves: 1
Equipment: oven-safe skillet (cast iron works great) or a small skillet plus a small baking sheet

Ingredients
- 1 bone-in, skin-on chicken thigh (about 6–7 oz / 170–200 g). If you have boneless skinless thighs, use one piece and reduce oven time.
- 1 small potato (about 5 oz / 140–150 g), cut into roughly 1-inch pieces
- 1/2 cup baby carrots or 3/4 cup green beans, trimmed
- 1 garlic clove, minced
- 1 tablespoon olive oil (divided)
- 1/2 lemon, juice (about 1 tablespoon) and zest optional
- 1/2 teaspoon dried thyme or rosemary (or your favorite herb)
- 1/4 teaspoon salt, 1/8 teaspoon black pepper (adjust to taste)
- Optional garnish: chopped parsley and a lemon wedge

Instructions
1) Thawing prep (if needed): Thaw the chicken in the fridge overnight, or use a quick cold-water method: sealed bag in cold water for 1–2 hours, changing water every 30 minutes.
2) Preheat oven to 425°F (220°C).
3) Prep potaotes and veg: toss the potato pieces with 1/2 teaspoon olive oil, a pinch of salt and pepper. If using carrots, slice them into 1/2-inch coins; if using green beans, trim them.
4) Season the chicken: pat the thigh dry with a paper towel. Rub with the remaining 1/2 tablespoon olive oil, salt, pepper, and the dried herb.
5) Sear the chicken: heat a skillet over medium-high heat. Add a teaspoon of oil if your pan is very dry. Place the chicken skin-side down and sear 4–5 minutes until the skin is deep golden and releasing easily from the pan.
6) Add vegetables and garlic: flip the chicken briefly, then scatter the potatoes and carrots/green beans around the chicken. Sprinkle minced garlic over everything.
7) Roast: transfer the skillet to the oven. Roast about 18–22 minutes for bone-in thighs (check doneness). The chicken should reach 165°F (74°C) in the thickest part. If you have boneless thighs, start checking at about 15–18 minutes.
8) Finish and serve: remove from oven, rest 5 minutes. Squeeze the lemon juice over the dish and (if you like) zest a little lemon over the top. Garnish with parsley if you have it.

Tips for a kitchen learner
- Mise en place: measure and prepare everything before you start cooking. This helps a lot when you’re learning.
- Dry the chicken well before seasoning to get crisper skin.
- Use a meat thermometer. 165°F (74°C) is the safe target for poultry.
- Rest the meat a few minutes after cooking; it stays juicier.
- Don’t overcrowd the pan. Plenty of space helps the chicken skin crisp up.
- If your pan isn’t oven-safe, sear the chicken on the burner, then transfer everything to a small baking dish to finish in the oven.
- Taste and adjust: a little extra lemon juice at the end can brighten the dish; a pinch more salt can wake up flavors.
